Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Kepler eccentricity and time-step controls Sixteen fixed evolutions at e=0.1/0.7 compare invariants, same-time phase error, physical periapsis times and reversal. Assumptions, units and boundaries a=mu=reduced mass=1, without softening. One-period runs use 512/1024/2048 steps; ten-period controls use h0=2π/2048. Variable steps use h=h0|q| at the current state, with only the final step shortened to the physical endpoint. Editorial clarification Small invariant errors do not establish phase accuracy. No canonical symplectic-defect measurement is claimed for the variable-step map, and fixed-h properties are not transferred automatically. R1 resolution was revised to R2 using pre-execution asymptotic planning, not measured calibration. Axes for trajectories, states, time or iterations do not represent physical spatial dimensions. Adopted numerical method Original central-force KDK Verlet. Fixed, replayed and regenerated schedules are distinct. Positive radial crossings of cubic Hermite trajectories are localized by brentq. q¨=−q/∥q∥3q¨​=−q/∥q∥3 E−esin⁡E=t,q=(cos⁡E−e,1−e2sin⁡E)E−esinE=t,q=(cosE−e,1−e2​sinE) H=12∥p∥2−1/∥q∥H=21​∥p∥2−1/∥q∥ References and measured quantities An independent Kepler-equation family, qualified with brentq and bisection, supports 92 main decisions: full-state error, energy/angular momentum, at least eight periapses, finite-window order and reversal defects. Verification limits and failures Small invariant errors do not establish phase accuracy. No canonical symplectic-defect measurement is claimed for the variable-step map, and fixed-h properties are not transferred automatically. R1 resolution was revised to R2 using pre-execution asymptotic planning, not measured calibration. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded.
